prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance toward the right rear corner and, pivoting on the left foot, reaps uke's right heel from the inside with the arch of the right foot, throwing uke backwards. Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall).

heading.en: Introductory way of applying the technique

prose.en: Uke's cooperation: Uke opens the right foot out and takes ushiro-ukemi (rear breakfall) supported on the left foot. Tori's cooperation: Tori pulls up on uke's right sleeve so that uke can take a solid ukemi. Uke opens the right foot forward, and tori reaps uke's right foot so as to open it out further, throwing uke to the rear. Uke works from a low posture up to a higher one by degrees: half-crouch → standing.

heading.en: Basic way of applying the technique

prose.en: Tori, using a forward tai-sabaki (body movement), breaks uke's balance to the rear and throws by reaping uke's right heel with the right foot.

Practising the direction of the reap Place the sole of the foot against uke's heel and check the effective direction of the reap. As practice for ushiro-ukemi, tori lets go of the pulling hand and uke slowly checks the rear breakfall.
Apply the technique with a rearward tai-sabaki (body movement) at the point where uke comes forward. Apply the technique with a forward tai-sabaki at the point where uke tries to step back.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori must not apply the technique with the hips pulled back. Tori must not apply the technique with the lifting hand (tsurite) fully extended.

When thrown, uke must not put the hand or elbow down on the mat. Do not fall together with uke. Tori stands firmly and pulls with the pulling hand (hikite). Uke does not cling to tori, but takes the ukemi (breakfall).

en: If tori overreaches and they fall together as one body, there is a risk that uke will be thrown straight backwards and strike the back of the head.
When ko-uchi-gari is applied to them, if uke twists the upper body and puts down a defending hand, there is a risk that uke will injure the wrist or elbow.

prose.en: Prohibit falling together as one body.

en: Instruct that, if tori loses balance, they release the lapel and sleeve of uke that they are holding so as not to fall together as one body. Uke can then more easily and safely take ukemi suited to the situation.
With a right-handed grip, instruct tori to draw uke's right sleeve in firmly and break uke's balance to the right rear corner before applying the technique.
Instruct uke to take ukemi cleanly without unreasonable defence.

し
○右組の場合、取（技をかける人）が右膝をつく低い状態で技をかけると、受（技
を受ける人）は真下に落ちやすく肩や肘を痛めることがあります。
○膝をつく低い状態で技をかけることは禁止しましょう。
○右組の場合、取は受を右前隅に崩して技をかけるようかかり練習や約束練習を繰り返して習熟を図
ることが重要です。
○取が自分のバランスを崩して膝をついた場合は、無理に投げようとしないで、持っている受の襟や
袖を放すように指導しましょう。そうすると受は状況に応じた受け身を安全にとりやすくなります。
○取が右組のまま左の体落としをかけると、受は左手を思わずついて手首や肘を
痛める原因となります。
○初心者の段階では右組のまま左の体落としをかけることを禁止し、必ず引き手の方向に投げるよう
指導しましょう。

腰
○取が腰を曲げて頭部を低くした状態で技をかけると、受ではなく、取が頭部か
ら突っ込み頸部を痛める恐れがあります。
○頭部を低くした状態で技をかけることを禁止し、自分のバランスを崩して低い姿勢になった場合は、
持っている受の襟や袖を放し、自ら前受け身をとるように指導しましょう。
○右組の場合、取は上体を起こし、受を右前隅に崩して技をかけるようかかり練習や約束練習を繰り
返して習熟を図ることが重要です。
